purpose: Keep GitHub useful for durable source/checkpoint coordination without making every content batch or runtime integration step depend on Git availability.
allowed_lightweight_automation: detect that portable/current workstream state is newer than Git metadata
write compact checkpoint/manifest metadata at a meaningful boundary
forbidden_or_default_off: commit per card or per lexical item
block content production until GitHub Actions completes
reconstruct/upload large checkpoint ZIPs through Git/Base64
deep Git history audit before every normal continuation
sync_triggers: handoff where durable metadata materially helps
coalescing_rule: If several content batches or runtime versions advance before the next sync boundary, synchronize the newest valid state directly; intermediate Git mirrors are not required when portable checkpoints preserve them.

turn_budget.on_failure: Record persistence.git=PENDING or FAILED, preserve artifact/hash/checkpoint/resume instructions, and continue production.

runtime_dependency_rule: Flashcards CURRENT may advance while Git mirror lags. Content integration targets CURRENT; Git lag never justifies fallback to LAST_FULLY_VERIFIED.
artifact_transport: Large ZIP/checkpoint artifacts stay in Library/Project/user-delivery; Git stores compact metadata/hashes/source.
